messages:
sam: FYI support escalation from AcmeApp — seeing a big p99 jump on /v1/generate starting ~2026-11-09T01:12Z. They report timeouts and a billing surprise. Link: https://grafana.company/r/abc123 (customer dashboard)
ops-bot: ALERT: route=/v1/generate p99 > 1500ms for 12m (now 2200ms), error rate 5% increased, hosts impacted: hostpool-gen-1
maria (sre): can you paste the grafana panels + which datasource? is this the aggregated quantile panel or the per-host histo? they look different.
sam: attached screenshots in ticket — panel is the "p99 (panel)" we use in customer-facing dashboard (uses series by host then quantile). customer also sent raw request traces showing many 401s then retries.
alex (observability): quick check — metric we're using for p99 is http_request_duration_seconds_bucket. dashboard panel is doing per-series quantile then avg, not a true aggregated histogram_quantile. that will understate tail when a few hosts have heavy tails. run this in grafana promql explorer:

```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le))
```

and compare to the per-host approach we had before.
maria (sre): good call. also check aggregation window — the dashboard is 1m, but the rollup we ship to the service tier uses 5m buckets which can produce different quantiles during spikes.
irene (platform): timeline note — we rotated the auth signing key at 2026-11-09T01:00Z (canary -> global). rollout was 100% at 01:04Z. any chance some SDKs hit old token behavior?
sam: customer logs show a pattern: 401 -> client retry -> success on 2nd/3rd try. they blamed us for increased token usage and billing. sample log snippet from customer:

```
[2026-11-09T01:12:03Z] POST /v1/generate 401 12ms x-request-id=...
[2026-11-09T01:12:03Z] RETRY 1 -> /v1/generate 200 2100ms x-request-id=...
[2026-11-09T01:12:05Z] RETRY 2 -> /v1/generate 200 2300ms x-request-id=...
```

sam: you can see retries are inflating both p99 (long tail) and token usage.
alex (observability): that log pattern will absolutely push p99 up: a small fraction of requests hit 401 then pay the latency cost of retries. Also, if retrying clients are concurrent, they create bursts that aggravate batching and KV cache misses — that amplifies the tail.
maria (sre): I pulled traces for a few sample request ids — the slow spans are the second/third attempt, not the initial 401. So the p95 stays OK but p99 jumps (classic retry tail).
ops-bot: Host-level anomaly: hostpool-gen-1 has new kernel patch applied 01:05Z — but cpu/mem usage normal. no OOMs.
irene (platform): we did a rolling kernel tweak in the same window (unrelated), but rollback would be heavier. leaning toward an auth-related root cause.
billing-bot: FYI billing estimate: increased requests from AcmeApp + retries => approx +2.6x billable tokens for the time window 01:10-01:40Z. temporary credit request flagged.
alex (observability): two-pronged investigation: 1) confirm that dashboard calc is hiding the true aggregated p99 (we need histogram_quantile over sum by le) 2) confirm auth rotation produced 401 bursts and client retries.
maria (sre): i ran the promql — aggregated histogram_quantile(0.99) shows p99 ~ 2100ms, matches customer traces. per-host quantile panel shows ~900ms. so it's a metric-surface mismatch + real spike.
sam: customer asks for repro steps and mitigation. can we reproduce internally?
alex (observability): quick repro: use a script that simulates half bad auth then retries with client backoff aggressive. e.g.:

```
# naive repro (do not run against prod publicly)
TOKEN=bad_token
for i in {1..100}; do \ 
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood/test/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' &\ 
done
```

then switch to good token for half of requests to mimic rotation. that produces 401->retry patterns and the tail.

maria (sre): short-term mitigations we can apply now:
- temporarily re-enable old token acceptance for 10m (fast rollback)
- add server-side small-window rate-limit on repeated retries per remote IP / api-key (protects against tight clients)
- update dashboard to show aggregated histogram_quantile and raw histogram panel for oncall
- change alert to trigger on histogram shape change (e.g., 99th - 95th delta > 800ms) instead of only raw p99

irene (platform): we can re-open old token for 10m — I'll prepare a short-lived feature flag. but we should also push a guidance note to customers re: client retry backoff.
sam: can we also offer AcmeApp a temporary credit while we sort this? billing-bot?
billing-bot: support-esc: provisional credit OK up to $5000; send request ID and time window. we'll reconcile if root cause on our side.

alex (observability): medium-term items (post-incident):
- instrument and expose per-route retry counts in graphs
- add synthetic test that exercises token rotation to detect replay/retry spikes during rollout
- make default dashboard quantile use aggregated histogram to avoid underreporting tail
- add canary gating for auth rotation (keep old token accepted until client ack seen)

maria (sre): immediate ops checklist (I'll own):
1) enable old token for 10m (irene) — do NOT announce publicly yet
2) flip dashboard to aggregated histo view for the oncall dashboard (alex)
3) add temporary rate-limit rule for repeated 401-then-retry patterns (platform)
4) send customer a short RCA + offer credit + mitigation plan (sam + billing)

irene (platform): doing step 1 now, ETA 3m. will post when flag is live.

ops-bot: action logged: incident-1959997777 created, severity P2, owners: maria, irene, sam.

sam: thx. i'll tell AcmeApp we're working on mitigation and will follow up with a detailed timeline and credit. :thumbsup:

maria (sre): followup postmortem items assigned. will update thread after dashboard change and metrics re-run.

alex (observability): one more note — when we fix dashboards, let's add a brief blurb in the panel tooltip: "This panel uses aggregated histogram_quantile across instances; use per-host panels to debug noisy hosts." avoids future confusion.

sam: closing loop: AcmeApp acknowledged temporary mitigation plan. will keep thread updated.

maria (sre): last message for now — p99 back to ~900ms after old token flag applied? we'll monitor. if it stays low, we'll coordinate a staged auth rollout with canary gating.

ops-bot: ALERT CLEAR: p99 for /v1/generate back under 1000ms (5m window)
